chief_complaint: Diabetes mellitus type 2 with chronic kidney disease and hypertension management
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 60‑year‑old Asian female with a long history of metabolic disease. Prediabetes was documented in 1983, progressing to overt type 2 diabetes in 2014. Hypertension and metabolic syndrome were diagnosed in 2015, followed by obesity, hypertriglyceridemia and non‑proliferative diabetic retinopathy in 2015. Microalbuminuria and stage 2 chronic kidney disease were identified in September 2020. She continues to smoke daily (40‑year history) and reports ongoing stress, limited social contact, and intimate‑partner abuse. Current vital signs show isolated diastolic hypertension (113/94 mmHg). Laboratory data are incomplete; the most recent HbA1c is recorded as 3 % (likely erroneous). She is on insulin, metformin, lisinopril, amlodipine and a nicotine patch, but lacks guideline‑directed therapies such as a statin or SGLT‑2 inhibitor. Psychosocial factors and refugee status further complicate adherence and follow‑up.
